content.title: UCLA beats Texas to advance to first NCAA women's national title game
content.text: April 3, 2026Updated April 4, 2026, 2:12 a.m. ETPHOENIX — The UCLA women’s basketball team has advanced to its first NCAA Tournament championship game.Texas rallied to within three late but Lauren Betts got a big block with 18.1 seconds to go on a would-be Madison Booker layup to help the Bruins held on in in a defensive battle, 51-44, on Friday night at Mortgage Matchup Arena. They will face South Carolina, which ended UConn’s 54-game winning streak in the first semifinal, in the title game on at 3:30 p.m. ET on Sunday."My job today was help in any way I can inside the paint," Betts said with a smile when asked about the block. "... As soon as I saw her getting downhill, I'm like, all right, please block this, just don't let her score."Betts, who transferred to UCLA after spending her freshman season at Stanford, had a double-double. She had 16 points and 11 rebounds to go with three blocks.Neither team shot particularly well, with the Bruins making 41% of her shots from the field and Texas 31%. Texas kept it close with good defense, turning UCLA over 23 times and turning it into 15 points."It definitely was not a pretty game," Close said. "I wanted to apologize to all the fans for the rugby match and the 23 turnovers."But I think credit to them, that they played that hard to force that kind of game. They have some just excellent players on their team. Lots of respect for the year that they had and how much challenge they provided."The Longhorns also had turnover troubles with 12 of their own. Booker also struggled with her shot, making only 3-of-23 from the field."It kind of did surprise me when I couldn't get out of my funk," Booker said. "It felt like every shot I put up, it felt like it was going to be money. But no, I think my teammates did a great job today at just making sure my spirits were high, my confidence was still high. Every shot, I shot it with confidence."I wished a few more fell in, not just for me but for my teammates, too. But yeah, it did feel kind of weird."Texas point guard Rori Harmon, who had eight points, five rebounds, five assists and four steals, came to Booker's defense."We want her to take those shots. There is another player on the other team that is 6-7," Harmon said "... I truly told Maddy, I don't care. I don't care what your statistics look like. There was plenty of other things that caused us to lose the game, not just because Madison missed her money midrange."I promise you we'll continue to go back to her, we'll continue to look for her, we'll continue to tell her to take her shot."The Longhorns, who lost in the national semifinals for the second straight season, finish 35-4.USA TODAY Sports is providing live updates and highlights of the Women's Final Four matchup between No. 1 UCLA and No. 1 Texas. Follow live updates here: UCLA vs Texas live score updatesThe Bruins have stretched their lead to 11 points with four minutes to go, 45-34. Texas coach Vic Schaefer has his jacket off and is red-faced on the sidelines.UCLA started its surge earlier in the quarter when Kiki Rice hit a 3-pointer to put the Bruins up 36-28. Then, Gabriela Jaquez made layup to give the Bruins the biggest lead of the game at 10 points, 38-28.Jaquez is into double figures with 10 points. End of Q3: UCLA 31, Texas 28This is not the offensive performance anyone who is a fan of women's basketball wanted to see. But the game is close. UCLA is shooting 35% and UCLA 28%. The two teams combined for 22 points in the third quarter.Lauren Betts is the lone player in double figures with 10 points. The senior center also has 10 rebounds and two blocks.Rori Harmon has eight points to lead the Longhorns. Madison Booker is 1-for-16.UCLA is looking to advance to its first championship game. UCLA's Lauren Betts hits headUCLA center Lauren Betts collided with Madison Booker, fell backwards and hit her head on the hardwood. She got up after several minutes and said she was OK. She is back playing and just hit a layup to put the Bruins up 26-19. Halftime: UCLA 20, Texas 17Neither team shot particularly well in the first half. UCLA is making 38% of its shots compared to 25% for Texas. Longhorns forward Madison Booker is 1-for-12 from the field in the first half.Gianna Kneepkens leads UCLA with seven points and Lauren Betts has six. Madison Booker stone coldTexas forward Madison Booker is shooting 1-of-11 from the field. The Longhorns are a hitting 27% of their shots and trailing 20-15.Harmon is carrying Texas with eight points early. Lauren Betts starting dominate insideUCLA senior center Lauren Betts is up to six points on 3-of-5 shooting and has four rebounds and a block. End of Q1: UCLA 14, Texas 6The Bruins are shooting 46% from the field in the early going to jump out to an eight-point lead. Gianna Kneepkens has five points and Lauren Betts four points. UCLA has held Texas to 21% shooting. Rori Harmon has four points. UCLA up earlyGianna Kneepkens has five points in the early going as the Bruins have jumped out to a 12-4 lead. We are way in PhoenixMadison Booker has Texas out to a 2-0 lead in the opening minute. Women's Final Four X-factorsAngela Dugalić opted to come off the bench for UCLA and the decision has paid dividends for both the Bruins and the Big Ten Women’s Basketball Sixth Player of the Year. Dugalić is a 6-foot-4 forward, but has the skillset of a guard. She creates instant mismatches, spreads the floor and brings a different level of intensity. Here's four X-factors players that can be key to national title. UCLA vs Texas women's basketball prediction UCLA will win Final Four game vs Texas if...Mitchel Northam: The Bruins need their guards to make 3-pointers to clear things out inside for Lauren Betts to go to work.Nancy Armour: Lauren Betts is going to need to assert herself early or Texas will run over UCLA.Meghan Hall: If it takes away Madison Booker's midrange game; It controls the glass.Heather Burns: If it runs its offense from the inside out, everything through Lauren Betts. Texas will win Final Four game vs UCLA if...Mitchel Northam: If the Longhorns start fast like they did against Kentucky and Michigan and build a double-digit lead early, theyll be tough to beat.Nancy Armour: If Rori Harmon can dictate the game as she did in their meeting earlier this season, Texas wins again.Meghan Hall: It contests every shot; It takes away the perimeter shooting from UCLA.Heather Burns: It forces keeps UCLA from scoring in the paint. Locking down Lauren Betts is the key. Lauren Betts watched UCLA's 2025 Final Four loss 10 times. Here’s what she learnedLauren Betts has UCLA women's basketball's 2025 Final Four loss to UConn seared into her brain.The 6-foot-7 center watched the Bruins' 34-point blowout loss to the eventual national champion Huskies at least 10 times, revealing her anger and confusion was the motivating factor behind her continually pressing rewind. Betts has since retired the footage and doesn't remember the last time she's watched it, but the loss has served as extra motivation as the Bruins returns to the Final Four in Phoenix in Friday."I knew I just wanted to get back here again. This is not the end goal. We want to keep playing two more games," Betts said on Thursday. "At the end of the day, our senior season is on the line. We want this so bad."Read Cydney Henderson's full story here. Texas reveals why coach's 'soft' criticism sparked Women's Final Four runIn February, Texas coach Vic Schaefer questioned the "heart" of his players after a blowout loss to Vanderbilt. "We had no heart tonight. We had no toughness. No competitive spirit. We're soft," Schaefer said at the time. The Longhorns' coach's words cut deep for his players, and forward Madison Booker knows it won't happen anymore. ""We turned it around. We got together as a team," she said. Meghan L. Hall's full story here. Madison Booker is 'like a sister' to Kevin DurantThe No. 35 symbolizes excellence for Texas basketball. Specifically the bucket-getting type. Kevin Durant rocked that number during his lone college season in Austin, which resulted in him becoming the first freshman to win Naismith Player of the Year. The Longhorns would later retire No. 35 for the men's program.Then came Madison Booker. The 6-foot-1 forward took No. 35 in 2023 and lived up to its lofty reputation, leading Texas to the Elite Eight while having to play point guard following Rori Harmon's torn ACL. She's proceeded to put together two superb seasons at her natural position, and with Harmon healthy again, the Longhorns are once again in the Final Four. Read Wajih AlBaroudi's story here.
